home.practice_assembly_blurb: Move parts the way each one moves and fit them to blueprints. Set several up, then fit them one after another for a chain.
assembly.title: Assembly
assembly.how_to: Each part moves its own way: a girder swaps sideways, a strut up or down, a cable corner to corner. A panel moves only when a part beside it swaps with it, and a core never moves. Drag a part onto a neighbour to swap them. Then pick a blueprint in the tray and drop it where the bay holds its parts: they are fitted and new parts appear in their place. A fit of n parts scores 10 for each part over two.
assembly.how_to_keyboard: Arrows move the cursor. Space picks the part under it, then an arrow, or Q, E, Z or C for a corner, swaps it that way. Number keys pick a blueprint; space or enter fits it with its top left on the cursor.
assembly.chain_note: Fits made one after another with no swap between are a chain: the second pays double, the third triple, up to six times. A swap ends the chain.
assembly.core_note: A core never moves, and in a blueprint it stands for any part. Each core a fit takes pays 10, times its place in the chain.
assembly.hint_note: Practice rounds show a move worth making when you pause.
assembly.legend_parts: Parts: each one's shape shows the way it moves.
assembly.legend_tray: The tray under the bay holds the blueprints. Pick one, then drop it where the bay holds its parts.
assembly.kind.panel: Panel. Has no way of its own: moves only when a neighbour swaps with it.
assembly.kind.core: Core. Never moves; stands for any part in a blueprint.
assembly.stage.parts_intro: Swap each part the way it moves, and fit blueprints. Bigger blueprints are worth more.
assembly.stage.chains_intro: Set several blueprints up, then fit them one after another: each fit in a chain pays more than the last.
assembly.stage.full_intro: Cores join the bay. They never move, and stand for any part.
